subject: Cost anomaly detected: $1,940 above expected spend
snippet: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection has identified unusual spend on your account (842-119-4471). Anomaly summary Total impact: $1,940.22 above the expected range Detection window: Jul 8 – J
body_text:
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection has identified unusual spend on your account (842-119-4471).

Anomaly summary
Total impact: $1,940.22 above the expected range
Detection window: Jul 8 – Jul 13, 2026
Root service: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)
Root cause candidates: instance class change, storage autoscaling, or a runaway query pattern

Daily breakdown
Jul 8:  $198.40 (expected $210.10)
Jul 9:  $204.15 (expected $208.90)
Jul 10: $612.88 (expected $215.30) ← anomaly starts
Jul 11: $701.04 (expected $217.65)
Jul 12: $588.19 (expected $219.02)
Jul 13: $541.77 (expected $221.40)

What changed
Our detection model flags this as most consistent with an instance class change on db-ingest-primary (db.r6g.xlarge → db.r6g.2xlarge) combined with a storage autoscaling event that added 400 GB of gp3 storage on Jul 10 at 03:14 UTC. Provisioned IOPS also increased from 3,000 to 9,000, which alone accounts for roughly $310 of the daily delta.

We also observed a sustained increase in ReadIOPS starting Jul 9 that correlates with deploy kettlehq/ingest-api#479 ("Backfill trace retention for enterprise tier"), which began a full-table backfill against the traces partition. If this backfill is still running, pausing it may reduce spend immediately; if it has completed, consider reverting the instance class once the backfill job's queue is drained, since day-to-day load does not appear to require the larger instance.

Recommended next steps
1. Confirm whether the ingest-api backfill (PR #479) is finished.
2. Review whether db-ingest-primary needs to remain at db.r6g.2xlarge or can step back down to db.r6g.xlarge.
3. Check storage autoscaling thresholds — 400 GB in three days is a fast ramp for a database that historically grows about 15 GB/week.

Projected impact if unaddressed
At the current daily delta of roughly $350-450 above baseline, this anomaly alone would add an estimated $10,500-$13,500 to the August bill if it runs for the full month, on top of the general upward trend already visible since the Lumenpay enterprise rollout began sending a larger volume of trace writes. Combined with last month's EC2 and S3 growth, July's run-rate would put you meaningfully ahead of the $12,000/month infra budget line that Wendy is trying to lock for the FY26 plan, which is worth flagging before the board meeting on Aug 27 if it isn't resolved by then.

This anomaly has been added to your Cost Explorer dashboard under Anomalies. You will receive a follow-up notification if daily spend returns to the expected range for three consecutive days.

View full anomaly report: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/home#/anomaly-detection

You are receiving this email because cost anomaly alerts are enabled for account 842-119-4471. To change your notification preferences, visit the Cost Management console.

meta.action_summary: Dev needs to check whether the ingest-api backfill (PR #479) finished and right-size db-ingest-primary back down.

subject: Open enrollment starts Monday — here's what's changing
snippet: Hi Maya, Open enrollment for Kettle's 2026-2027 benefits plan year opens Monday, August 10th and runs through Friday, August 21st. Here's a summary of what's changing so you can he
body_text:
Hi Maya,

Open enrollment for Kettle's 2026-2027 benefits plan year opens Monday, August 10th and runs through Friday, August 21st. Here's a summary of what's changing so you can help answer questions if employees ask.

Medical
We're moving from Anthem to Kaiser Permanente as the primary HMO option and adding a second PPO tier through Anthem for employees who want broader out-of-network coverage. Premiums for the base HMO plan are essentially flat (up about 2.1%), but the new PPO tier runs roughly 34% higher than the HMO on a per-employee basis. Company contribution stays at 85% of the HMO premium regardless of which plan an employee picks, so anyone moving to the PPO will see a bigger chunk taken from their paycheck.

Dental and vision
No changes to the dental plan (Guardian). Vision is switching carriers from VSP to EyeMed, which should be a lateral move in terms of coverage but the provider network is different, so anyone with a regular eye doctor should double check they're still in-network before the switch takes effect Oct 1.

401(k)
The employer match is increasing from 3% to 4% of salary effective the first payroll of the new plan year, which the board approved as part of the Series A comp refresh. No action needed from employees to receive the higher match — it applies automatically to anyone already contributing.

HSA/FSA
HSA contribution limits are increasing per the IRS 2027 figures ($4,300 individual / $8,550 family). FSA limits are also increasing slightly to $3,300.

What we need from you
As CEO, you don't need to do anything for your own enrollment beyond the standard elections, but Wendy may loop you in if there are questions about the PPO tier cost during the all-hands Q&A on August 12th. Happy to join that meeting if useful, especially since the option pool and comp refresh questions tend to come up in the same breath as benefits questions once people start comparing total compensation.

Timeline
Aug 10: Enrollment opens, portal live
Aug 12: All-hands Q&A session, 11am Pacific
Aug 19: Reminder email to anyone who hasn't enrolled
Aug 21: Enrollment closes at 11:59pm Pacific
Oct 1: New plan year and carrier changes take effect

One more note on timing: because the vision carrier switch (VSP to EyeMed) takes effect Oct 1 rather than at the start of enrollment, anyone with an eye appointment scheduled between now and then should double check their provider is in-network under the outgoing VSP plan, not the incoming EyeMed one — we've seen this trip people up in past years when the two dates don't line up.

Full plan comparison and rate sheets are attached to the enrollment portal at https://app.rippling.com/benefits/enrollment. If you or anyone on the team has questions before then, our support team is available at benefits-support@rippling.com or through the chat widget in the portal.

Best,
The Rippling Benefits Team

subject: Weekly error budget report: ingest-api
snippet: Your weekly SLO report for ingest-api (Jul 24 – Jul 31) is ready. Summary SLO target: 99.9% availability (30-day rolling) Current attainment: 99.86% Error budget remaining: 34% (10
body_text:
Your weekly SLO report for ingest-api (Jul 24 – Jul 31) is ready.

Summary
SLO target: 99.9% availability (30-day rolling)
Current attainment: 99.86%
Error budget remaining: 34% (10h 12m of the 30-day budget)
Trend: down from 61% remaining last week

What burned the budget this week
Three events accounted for nearly all of this week's burn. The largest was a 41-minute partial outage on Jul 28 (see incident #4459) caused by a connection pool exhaustion issue when the enterprise trace-view feature flag was enabled for Lumenpay's tenant, driving a 6x increase in concurrent queries against the read replica. The second was an 18-minute degradation on Jul 29 tied to the same root cause recurring after a partial rollback. The third was a smaller 6-minute blip on Jul 30 during the nightly backfill job.

Endpoint breakdown
POST /v1/traces/ingest      99.94% (target 99.9%) — healthy
GET  /v1/traces/query       98.71% (target 99.9%) — driving the miss
GET  /v1/dashboards/:id     99.98% (target 99.9%) — healthy
POST /v1/alerts/webhook     99.99% (target 99.9%) — healthy

The query endpoint is the clear outlier and matches the connection pool story above — trace-view queries hit the same replica as the standard dashboard queries and don't yet have their own connection pool or rate limit.

Recommendation
If the trace-view flag stays on for more enterprise tenants before a dedicated connection pool ships, we expect the budget to fully deplete before the 30-day window resets, which would put the team in breach of the customer-facing SLA with Lumenpay and Tarrow Health. Suggest either pausing the trace-view rollout to additional tenants or fast-tracking the connection pool work (tracked as KET-461) ahead of the currently planned Cycle 16 slot.

Historical context
This is the second week in a row the query endpoint has been the primary driver of budget burn — last week it landed at 99.90%, right at the edge of target, and the week before that it was comfortably above target at 99.97%. The trend lines up with the trace-view flag being enabled for Lumenpay on Jul 18 and then for Tarrow Health on Jul 25, which roughly doubled the number of tenants hitting the shared query path. If a third enterprise tenant is enabled before the connection pool work ships, we'd expect the query endpoint to fall below 99% for the week, which would fully exhaust the remaining 34% of budget well before the 30-day window resets on Aug 23.

Full dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/slo/ingest-api-availability
Incident history: https://app.datadoghq.com/incidents?q=ingest-api

meta.action_summary: Priya needs to decide whether to pause the trace-view rollout or fast-track the connection pool fix (KET-461) before the SLO budget fully depletes.
